quest.title: Perfect Send-Off
quest.description: It turns out that Big G's spirit was attracted by the exorcism. Upon learning that Big G has not become a malevolent spirit and simply wanted to check on Meng and other childhood friends, Hu Tao decides to fulfill his wish and organize a farewell ceremony for him. To give him peace of mind, you collect keepsakes and well-wishes that Big G's childhood friends prepared for him. The only thing left now is to send him off.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Primogem x60, Mora x41750, Guide to Diligence x5, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x9

talks.objective: Take the keepsakes to Wuwang Hill and give them to Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Oh! You're back already? Sooner than I expected!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: You didn't go spilling the beans, did you, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does Paimon look that unreliable to you?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, I'm kidding. Anyway, looks like they were willing to hand over some keepsakes, so I guess they knew the deal.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Nevertheless, when it comes to things like ghosts and ghouls, spirits and souls, the one thing everyone knows is you never know what to expect...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Which explains why they were reluctant to pry and find out the full story. Which is just as well — because if they had attempted to... it would have been too much for me to deal with.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: "Guard the border between life and death..." This is Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's most important responsibility. And I'm stricter than most...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what about us? Does it matter if we cross the "border"?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Of course not. After all, you were caught up in all this already, just like Meng. It's not the end of the world if you catch a glimpse behind the curtain.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: And where we're going, don't be surprised at what you may see or what may occur.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: All of it exists within the border between the living and the dead, an ordinary place, really. The only special thing about it is that nobody really knows about it.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Whatever you do, don't get all worked up over nothing, okay? Or else by the time we're out, I'll have to erase your memories.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So, listen to everything I say. Let's go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: P—Paimon's scared...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But like Hu Tao says, we're already caught up in this. We'd better see it through to the end.

choices.text: I can't tell if you're serious anymore.

talks.objective: Go to the "ordinary place" mentioned by Hu Tao

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally! Paimon thought we were gonna be trapped in that weird place forever!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: That's exactly the point. Trespassers end up running scared.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So that's the weird stuff out of the way, right?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Yep, just dive off the edge here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wahhhh!?

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Wow, there are even the names of all five of us on it!

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Hehe, amazing. Oh, didn't you just say that you release lanterns every year? Do you plan to add more names over the years?

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Like Little Wu's kids and Mumu's wife?

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Actually, I have some good news. Mumu is soon to be a father. He's been talking about nothing else recently. He's excited and nervous at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Hahaha, I wonder if such a goofball will make a good father.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: No, no, no, you'd be surprised how sharp-witted he is now. Let me tell you...

talks.objective: Follow the path to the border
Continue forward to witness the farewell ceremony

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu (Memory)
dialogues.text: It's the Lantern Rite again. Wouldn't it be cool if we got to see the lanterns ourselves one day?

dialogues.speaker: Congzi (Memory)
dialogues.text: You can make a wish without a lantern, you know. My mom told me — as long as you yell it really loud, your wish will come true in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Big G (Memory)
dialogues.text: Yell it? Isn't that... kinda embarrassing?

dialogues.speaker: Meng (Memory)
dialogues.text: As soon as the first person yells, then everyone else just joins in, and nobody feels embarrassed anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi (Memory)
dialogues.text: That's right. Little Wu, you start.

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu (Memory)
dialogues.text: Alright... I—I wish I could open a massive restaurant, with never-ending dishes and snacks, so I could eat Jueyun Chili Chicken every day!

dialogues.speaker: Mumu (Memory)
dialogues.text: Hahaha, that's your wish?

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu (Memory)
dialogues.text: If that's so funny, what's your wish?

dialogues.speaker: Mumu (Memory)
dialogues.text: To get rich of course! Do big business and make a load of Mora! With Mora, you can do whatever you want and be happy!

dialogues.speaker: Meng (Memory)
dialogues.text: Yeah, if you get rich you could buy that super expensive toybox.

dialogues.speaker: Mumu (Memory)
dialogues.text: Not just one... One for everyone — no, loads for everyone!

dialogues.speaker: Congzi (Memory)
dialogues.text: Well, if Mumu's gonna be a businessman, then I don't need to earn any money.

dialogues.speaker: Mumu (Memory)
dialogues.text: Whoa whoa whoa, it's tough getting rich. Don't put all the pressure on me!

dialogues.speaker: Congzi (Memory)
dialogues.text: As for me, I want to learn to make Mingxiao Lanterns, the big kind! And Xiao Lanterns too. I'll be the best artisan around.

dialogues.speaker: Big G (Memory)
dialogues.text: Yeah, that way we don't need to go to Liyue Harbor to release Xiao Lanterns!

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu (Memory)
dialogues.text: Anyway, those are our wishes. Meng, Big G, what about you?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, they all disappeared... right when he was about to make his wish.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: It brings back so many memories! That was the last Lantern Rite the five of us spent together.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: It's been so long... Everyone's all grown up...

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Have all of those wishes really come true?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We asked each of them for parting gifts for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Little Wu's become a chef, Mumu's a successful businessman, and Congzi makes great Xiao Lanterns.

response.speaker: Big G
response.text: Really...

response.speaker: Big G
response.text: Wow...

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: We've never forgotten our childhood dreams. We've kept them in our hearts as a promise to each other.

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Anyway. Time to release this lantern.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: #Hey {NICKNAME}, take a hint.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Let's give them some space to go over the good old days.

choices.text: We can prove it to you.

talks.objective: Talk to Hu Tao while the old friends are reminiscing

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Take the hint"? Really? Of all of us, you're the one who needs to learn how to read the room.

choices.text: Don't you need to "guard the border"?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Meng's already crossed the "border," that's the only way to send Big G off.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: As I explained, Wangsheng Funeral Parlor was, once upon a time, more akin to a doctor's office than an actual funeral parlor.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: During the Archon War, piles of corpses covered the wilderness. People were plunged into misery and suffering. Disease was spreading all over the land. Death devastated the world of the living.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Such were the times when the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor was first established. As humans, its founders were deemed too insignificant to matter, but slowly, they managed to drive away death.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They must've paid a huge price for that.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: After generations, Liyue Harbor became a bustling hub of prosperity, luring people with dreams of great fame and abundant Mora. But in the end, some lunatics stirred up the "legacy" of the dead.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: By that, I mean the remnants of the defeated gods that ravaged the world. I won't go into specifics of that situation, but suffice to say that at its peak, life was on the verge of bringing about its own extinction, while death was coming back with a vengeance.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: It took a long, long time, longer than you'd think, to restore balance and reinstate the "border." Without it, Liyue Harbor as we know it wouldn't be here today — neither would the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, you, or me.

choices.text: I didn't expect you to be such a storyteller.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hahaha, the previous directors all loved to tell this one, too. Although, if you ask me, I think I tell it best.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: What you make of my words is up to you. I do hope that most of it flew over your heads, though. The Wangsheng Funeral Parlor is just that, a funeral parlor. Nothing more to it.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: We live in peaceful times, but this harmonious coexistence between life and death should never be taken for granted.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Huh, it's about time. Let's go! Let's take them to "the place where all begins and all goes to rest"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What kind of place is that?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I just mean where we first bumped into each other. I come up with fun names for things sometimes, okay? No need to hound me with questions about every little thing I say!

choices.text: Won't disagree. It's time to go back.
Can you reveal a bit more?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Not a chance! Curiosity can be perilous, you know. Don't forget my warning, the less you know, the better.

choices.text: Your scope of work is nothing like I imagined.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Really? The end result is the same, though. Exactly what I do and how I do it are just minor technicalities.

talks.objective: Go back to Wuwang Hill to send Big G off

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: I think we did everything we could to make you happy, Big G, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: But... if you ever really do become an evil spirit and come back with more nefarious nonsense in mind, I may have to forget our friendship and give you a far less fond farewell...

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: I won't, I promise! ...I'm grateful for everything you've done for me.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Now that I know that my friends are doing so well, I have no intention to bother them.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I also want to thank you. You made my dream come true, too.

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: So you should also mind my warning, Meng. If you won't let go of the past, I might reunite you two sooner than you think.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: How can you say such horrendous things with that smile on your face...

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Hahaha, well then, last but not least, let's say our good-byes to Big G.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: See you later, Big G!

dialogues.speaker: Hu Tao
dialogues.text: Not like that! You won't be "seeing him later." Let's stick to "good bye" and such.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Hahaha, no worries. I'll just take my leave.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. Of all the wishes we yelled that day, only ours hasn't come true.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: Don't be bothered by that. No life is without its regrets. You can leave in peace now.

dialogues.speaker: Big G
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll remember you all... Good bye...

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: He's gone, then... *sigh*

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: I thought that closure would bring me relief, but all I can feel now is... emptiness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what was the wish you two made? We didn't have a chance to hear it earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: "After each of us has started a family and built a career, we want both our families to spend the Lantern Rite together."

dialogues.speaker: Meng
dialogues.text: That's why I envy my friends so much. Little Wu and the rest, they all had a chance to fulfill their wishes. Mine, however, will remain just a dream...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: That's right. Also, think about this: Everyone gets burnt to ash one day.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: So enjoy your life while you can, and when your duty to the living is over, you can meet whoever you want again in the afterlife. Isn't that great?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Uhhhh... Th—Thank you?

response.speaker: Meng
response.text: Either way, I don't think I'll ever return to Wuwang Hill. I have a lot of feelings to process.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: No worries, it's a good opportunity for you to go on vacation. Consider your leave approved. Ah, naturally, this doesn't change the terms of our previous agreement. The leave will be unpaid.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Aren't you forgetting about something?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You promised that you'll help us in our search.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I took you to the "border" and let you have a look around, didn't I? But based on your reaction, it seems like you didn't find what you're looking for. It's a pity, indeed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...The biggest pity of all is your lack of help!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hahaha, I was fishing around on your behalf through the channels that aren't accessible to you. Unfortunately, I didn't find any leads worth pursuing either.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: I'll keep my eyes open in case anything crops up. If so, I'll be sure to let you know.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't sound like you mean it...

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Hehe, I'm not an expert on tracking down the living. However, if you want me to summon someone from the other side of the "border"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Grr, stop saying creepy stuff!

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Relax! I'll help you look for them, you have my word. Tsk, my exquisite sense of humor always goes unappreciated.

choices.text: Seems like you really like your job.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: Haha... I have my reasons.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Reasons?

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: The spirits we saw near the border are the dead that still long for the world of the living.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: But I've never seen any of the previous directors there, not even once.

response.speaker: Hu Tao
response.text: This means that becoming the Director of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor was the right decision for them and left them with no regrets.

choices.text: Seems like being a funeral home director really suits you.
You still have a lot ahead of you.

dialogues.speaker: Mumu
dialogues.text: Y'know, I just realized... mine's the only item that's been outright purchased. Yours are both handmade.

dialogues.speaker: Little Wu
dialogues.text: But yours is worth a lot more.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi
dialogues.text: Worth in Mora is not what's important here. These things all played a big part in our childhood.

dialogues.speaker: Congzi
dialogues.text: They show that we will never forget our promise.

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: Are you... clients? Apologies, this is just a little unexpected.

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: Seeing that it was Hu Tao that brought you puts me at ease... But I'm afraid we don't have the means to entertain guests here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: My name is Lanxi, I've been waiting for someone for a long time now, exactly how long I couldn't really say.

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: Everyone says waiting is difficult, but walking, watching, talking to newcomers and the old crowd... It helps to pass the time.

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: I can keep waiting, but who knows whether what I'm waiting for will ever come to pass?

dialogues.speaker: Lanxi
dialogues.text: It's all the same to me, waiting's all I can do anyway. But if you, too, are looking for someone important to you, it's best not to keep waiting forever.

dialogues.speaker: Zhu Ming
dialogues.text: Are you new here? What a coincidence, so am I!

dialogues.speaker: Zhu Ming
dialogues.text: I can't believe how nice the scenery is! I thought it would be all pitch-black and freezing cold, with no sense of space or time!

dialogues.speaker: Zhu Ming
dialogues.text: Here I can finally work out a lifetime of emotions, it's fantastic. Haha, perhaps I just set my expectations too low.

dialogues.speaker: Shu'yang
dialogues.text: By the way, have you seen Uncle Zhang recently?

dialogues.speaker: Mo
dialogues.text: That guy? I remember him saying it was time for him to move on.

dialogues.speaker: Shu'yang
dialogues.text: Ah, good for him. I wonder where he's off to next?

dialogues.speaker: Mo
dialogues.text: If you're curious, why don't we go and see for ourselves?

dialogues.speaker: Shu'yang
dialogues.text: Haha, some other time perhaps. I'd like to stay here for a while.
